title: Flight of enslaved people from Attica during the Spartan occupation of Decelea
summary: Beginning in the spring of 413 BCE, after Sparta fortified the Attic deme of Decelea during the Peloponnesian War, more than twenty thousand enslaved people fled Athenian territory, a great part of them skilled artisans by Thucydides' account. The desertion deprived Athens of labour and income during its final struggle against Sparta.

uncertainty.note: Spartan fortification of Decelea began in the spring of 413 BCE (archon year 414/3 BCE) and the garrison remained until Athens surrendered in 404 BCE.

as_recorded.value: 414 (winter) Sparta reenters the war, following Alcibiades’s advice, takes and fortifies the deme of Decelea, encouraging Athenian slaves to escape
more than twenty thousand slaves had deserted, a great part of them artisans

where.historical_name: Dekeleia, Attic inland deme, fortified Spartan base in the Peloponnesian War

importance.justification: The mass flight of over twenty thousand enslaved laborers and artisans crippled Athenian silver mining and wartime finances, decisively altering the balance of the Peloponnesian War.

audience_note: Details ancient chattel slavery, forced mine labor at Laurion, and mass wartime desertion under Spartan occupation.

sources.title: The History of the Peloponnesian War, Book VII
sources.author: Thucydides; trans. Richard Crawley

beats.caption: In 413 BCE, Spartan forces under King Agis II fortify Decelea, establishing a permanent base in northern Attica.
More than twenty thousand enslaved artisans and miners flee Attica, devastating Athenian public revenue and manufacturing.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the exact proportion of runaway slaves employed in the Laurion silver mines versus urban craft workshops, as Thucydides specifies cheirotechnai broadly.
